functions.name: issues
functions.description: Canonical GitHub issues across authored, repository, label, filtered REST, authenticated participation and linked-issue retrieval. GraphQL node identity and field values stay consistent; REST Issue endpoints exclude pull requests before hydration. Authenticated participation is not authorship. Common lifecycle, rendered-body, sub-issue summary and milestone observations come from existing GraphQL selections. REST-only actor, assignee, type, reaction and dependency snapshots are NULL on GraphQL-only routes; adding fields never introduces an extra request. REST reaction and dependency counts and GraphQL sub-issue counts are upstream observations; no nested connection populations are selected or declared complete.

metrics.name: issue_count
metrics.comment: Canonical visible Issue identities in the explicitly selected route population. Pull requests are excluded. Authored routes prove authorship; participation and repository routes do not.

metrics.name: issue_active_days
metrics.comment: Distinct UTC creation dates represented by selected visible records. Non-additive across repositories and other overlapping groups; inactive dates contribute zero.

metrics.name: issue_repository_count
metrics.comment: Distinct known repository identities represented by selected visible records. Non-additive across dates/categories; unknown repository context is excluded.

derived_fields.name: issue_created_day
derived_fields.comment: UTC Gregorian day of creation; weeks begin Monday.

derived_fields.name: issue_created_week
derived_fields.comment: UTC Gregorian week of creation; weeks begin Monday.

derived_fields.name: issue_created_month
derived_fields.comment: UTC Gregorian month of creation; weeks begin Monday.

derived_fields.name: issue_title_category
derived_fields.comment: Transparent classification from case-insensitive conventional title prefixes docs:, fix:, feat:, refactor:, test:. First matching rule wins; other titles are unclassified. This describes title wording, not author intent; original title is available as evidence.

functions.name: commit_comments
functions.description: Commit comments authored by the selected user, not commits or code-change counts. Repository scope includes all authors; user scope selects authors; combining both intersects by canonical author identity. Repository and exact-commit REST listings share the canonical node grain with authored GraphQL. The additional numeric comment ID is nullable where GraphQL does not expose it. Commit SHA, path, position and author association preserve their pinned GraphQL equivalents; a deleted or inaccessible GraphQL commit association remains NULL. REST-only line and reaction-rollup metadata are not yet public canonical fields.
